left_out.FR sway bar + bushing (FR Swaybar (50k),: bar and bushing share a bench frame, but the bushing bracket has no STEP: its two bolt holes would have to be picked on the mesh to seat it on the subframe's M8 pair (Front Suspension.STEP, y=-281.8, x 1416/1508); without that the bar's axis height and its rotation are a guess

left_out.rear upper spring pad / perch as separat: duplicates of geometry already inside the Top + Bottom spring scans used for RR_spring
left_out.FR Coilover (4.2m) / Rear Shock (2.2m) /: fully extended bench state; replaced by their Top/Bottom sub-scans so the damper can telescope to ride height
left_out.LCA Sensor *: later add-on, not stock suspension (as instructed)

measured (STEP / scan features): wheel spin axis = bearing axis through the solved hub (point wheel_centre, direction spin_axis_outboard)

front steering axis = steer_axis_top (strut tower mount centre) -> steer_axis_bottom (LCA ball joint centre); note this is a double-joint axle: the true instantaneous lower pivot is the intersection of the LCA and tension-rod lines, so the kinematically exact motion is in steer_samples
front: lca_inner / tension_rod_inner bracket centres + bolt axes, ball centres, link lengths, strut axis, tie-rod inner/outer balls
rear: links{} inner bracket centres + axes, outer joints, lengths; damper top/eye; spring seat/pocket; sway-bar axis

travel_samples / steer_samples: exact mechanism solves at each step. Apply knuckle_group_delta (4x4, car frame) to every part in knuckle_group, arm_deltas[name] to each link (and to lca_wing, damper_body, spring bottom with the lca), keep body-fixed parts (top mounts, cv_inner, rack) still
sign conventions: camber_deg < 0 = top of the wheel leans inboard
toe_deg / steer_deg > 0 = front of the RIGHT wheel towards +y (toe-in on the right, i.e. a left turn); left-side values are mirrored
wheel_travel_mm > 0 = bump (wheel centre up relative to the body); rack_travel_mm > 0 = rack towards +y (left)
assumed: ride height = Ground Plane.STEP ground + 331 mm tyre radius (255/35R19 front, same radius used rear as in corners.py)
front toe = 0 at rack centre (tie-rod length is then an output: 340.4 mm, 30 mm thread engagement with the in-situ inner rod)
rack travel is applied as a pure y shift of the inner tie-rod ball
not determinable from the data: bump/droop limits (bump stop contact) - samples stop at the scanned full-extension strut (front droop -76 mm) and are otherwise open-ended
spring clocking about its own axis; bushing compliance; sway-bar preload
